name: Naama (Ammonite, mother of Rehoboam)
title: Solomon's Ammonite wife
summary: Naama was an Ammonite woman who became one of King Solomon's many wives. She is best known as the mother of Rehoboam, who succeeded Solomon as king over Judah. Her foreign origin is mentioned as part of Solomon's turning away from the Lord.

keyEvents.title: Marriage to Solomon
keyEvents.description: Naama was among the foreign women Solomon took as wives, which went against God's command not to marry women from pagan nations.

keyEvents.title: Mother of Rehoboam
keyEvents.description: Naama gave birth to Rehoboam, who would become the next king over Judah after Solomon's death. She is specifically mentioned as his mother in the royal records.

keyEvents.title: Mentioned in the history of the kings of Judah
keyEvents.description: When Rehoboam became king over Judah, Naama's Ammonite origin was explicitly noted, highlighting the foreign influence on the royal house.
